original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

actual_scope: State and prove the hub normal form (necessary and sufficient conditions, with no dyadic obstruction beyond invertibility over Z[1/2]) for the events at the zero and full frames of a P104 native word, an up-set crossing bound on private descents, the invariance of the invoice under scheduling, and the frame law for pair exchanges; check each exactly on the literal #6824 native word.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a source-bound construction. This package proves structure theorems about re-gauging the zero-frame and full-frame events of a native word and rewrites one word to show the freedom; it constructs no priced word and claims no kappa.
bottleneck_link: docs/research/research-family-status.md; the zero-frame and full-frame events of a native word carry no frame change and no invoice, and this package characterises exactly which mid maps admit such hubs.
stop_rule: No kappa claim. The rewritten word is a witness of a freedom, has more events than the original and is not re-priced; any application needs its own complete invoice and the five framework assumptions of the cited word.
evidence: PROOF.md (statements and proofs), verify.py (exact replay on the #6824 native word with controls and small instances), retained/SOURCE-PINS.json (input pin).

open_questions.question: Is a unimodular completion of the hub gauge always reachable with dyadic unit pivots, or only with a general Smith-type completion?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Theorem 3.2 proves existence over the principal ideal domain Z[1/2]; the replay uses a greedy unit-pivot rule that succeeded on the literal word.
open_questions.first_step: Search small random systems satisfying C1, C2, C2', C4 for a case where the greedy rule fails and compare with the Smith-form completion.
open_questions.blocked_by: Compute time only; no new mathematics is expected.

open_questions.question: Can a hub gauge at an intermediate frame (neither the zero nor the full frame) re-gauge more of the mid map?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The normal form is exact for gauges supported on K at {0} and on R at the full frame; the conditions C1, C2, C2' say what remains rigid.
open_questions.first_step: State the analogue of Theorem 3.1 for registers at rest at a frame F and test it on one frame of the literal word.
open_questions.blocked_by: A statement of which events of a mid map commute to a chosen frame.

open_questions.question: Does re-gauging the hubs change which pure dual pairs exist at interior cuts?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The hub gauge changes the prefix matrices at every interior cut, and the dual-pair criterion of #6827 reads those matrices.
open_questions.first_step: Compute the pure lattices of one helper class at one interior cut of the original and of the rewritten word.
open_questions.blocked_by: None; needs the pair lattices of #6827.
